title: What If You Started a Country on a Rusty Sea Fort? Someone Did

scenes.text: What if you could start your own country on a rusty sea fort? In 1967, a man did.
Roy Bates, a former British army major, moved onto HM Fort Roughs, a World War Two gun platform about seven miles off Suffolk.
Back then Britain's waters ended three miles from shore. In 1968 a British court said it had no jurisdiction over the fort.
Bates declared the Principality of Sealand, with its own flag, passports and stamps.
In 1978, German and Dutch businessmen stormed it while he was away. His family retook it and held them as prisoners.
Britain later widened its waters to twelve miles, which swallowed the fort. Nobody recognizes Sealand, and the family still holds it.

description:
What if you could start your own country on a rusty sea fort?
In 1967 Roy Bates, a former British army major, occupied HM Fort Roughs, a Second World War gun platform about seven miles off the Suffolk coast. At the time British waters ended three miles from shore, and in 1968 a British court ruled it had no jurisdiction over the fort. Bates declared the Principality of Sealand with its own flag, passports and stamps, and in 1978 his family retook it after a coup attempt by German and Dutch businessmen. Britain widened its waters to twelve miles in 1987 and no country formally recognizes Sealand.
What should we run through next?
